proposals.before: Let his son Yi be granted one hundred jin yellow gold, thereby to supply his sacrifices and worship."
proposals.after: Let Yi's son be granted one hundred jin yellow gold, thereby to supply his sacrifices and worship.
proposals.reason: 邑子 means the son of Zhu Yi (邑), not a son named Yi; the literal reverse-genitive misreads the kinship phrase.

proposals.before: Wen Weng came from Shu District in Lujiang Commandery.
proposals.after: Wen Weng came from Shu county in Lujiang Commandery.
proposals.reason: 廬江舒 is Shu county (舒) in Lujiang, not the Shu of Sichuan; "Shu District" invites confusion with 蜀.

proposals.before: At the time few could be praised for transforming and governing; only Chancellor of Jiangdu Dong Zhongshu, Imperial Household Grandee Gongsun Hong, and Ni Kuan were worth recording in office.
proposals.after: At the time few could be praised for transforming and governing; only Chancellor of Jiangdu Dong Zhongshu, Neishi Gongsun Hong, and Ni Kuan were worth recording in office.
proposals.reason: 內史 is the metropolitan Neishi, not well rendered as "Imperial Household Grandee"; keep the office title clear.

decisions.reason: Focus Chinese 其賜邑子黃金百斤 follows the edict on 大司農邑 (Zhu Yi); 邑子 is Yi's son, not a son named Yi. The proposed literal restores the correct kinship reading without changing the rest of the phrasing.

Focus Chinese 文翁，廬江舒人也 already places 舒 in Lujiang; idiomatic “Shu District in Lujiang Commandery” correctly identifies that native place and is disambiguated from Sichuan 蜀 by the commandery. Swapping District for county is a stylistic preference, not a meaning error.

decisions.after: At the time few could be praised for transforming and governing; only Chancellor of Jiangdu Dong Zhongshu, Capital Superintendent Gongsun Hong, and Ni Kuan were worth recording in office.
decisions.reason: Focus Chinese 內史公孫弘 names Gongsun Hong as neishi (metropolitan capital superintendent), not Imperial Household Grandee. The proposed bare “Neishi” is awkward English; revise to the natural office title already used in the idiomatic line.
